newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile pension funds seen investing $300 mln abroad.
newsitem.headline: Chile pension funds seen investing $300 mln abroad.

text.p: Chile's private pension funds could invest $300 million abroad in the first half of the year as part of a push to diversify their billion-dollar portfolios, said pension fund superintendent Julio Bustamante.
"We hope 1997 is the year when the pension funds take their money abroad," Bustamante told reporters.
Bustamante said he expected the funds to invest up to $1.5 billion in foreign markets over coming years, mainly through international investment funds which will start operating by mid-year.
"An attractive combination would be a mix of investments in developed and emerging markets," he said.
So far high local interest rates and wariness of foreign markets have meant that the funds, which control $27.5 billion, have invested a tiny 0.5 percent of their portfolios abroad.
The government also hopes the funds will also diversify by investing up to $4.2 billion in local infrastructure projects ranging from roads to ports, said Bustamante.
"We estimate funds can finance 35-40 percent of the total investments in infrastructure projects," he said.
The need to branch out has become pressing over the last two years as the result of the lackluster performance of the Santiago stock exchange, where the funds have a large part of their investments.
The funds posted a 3.5 percent return on assets last year, against a 2.5 percent loss in 1995.
The improvement was mainly the result of higher earnings from fixed income investments due to rising interest rates.
The system, which has been widely copied in Latin America, should report better results this year, provided the funds achieve a stronger mix of investments, said Bustamante.
"This year should be better than 1996 as a result of the process of diversification," said Bustamante.
